headline: SILVER REBOUNDS FROM 8-MONTH LOW AS GOLD HOLDS $4,000 FLOOR — Physical Buyers Absorb Iran-Oil Rate-Hike Pressure; XAG Eyes $57 Next
snippet: Spot silver rebounded to $56.80 from an 8-month low struck near $55 last week, outperforming gold as physical buyers returned to both metals despite Iran-driven oil prices pushing December Fed rate-hike probability on CME FedWatch to 73%. Gold held the $4,000 psychological floor — the key support level heading into the July 29 FOMC meeting — after the precious metals complex posted its sharpest monthly decline since Q2 2025.

headline: AWALÉ HITS 43.7 g/t AuEq AT 385m DEPTH BELOW BBM OPEN PIT — Highest Grade in Deposit History Signals Underground Growth at Odienné (TSXV: ARIC)
snippet: Awalé Resources (TSXV: ARIC) released the first two results from its 12-hole deep-drilling campaign at the BBM deposit in Côte d'Ivoire: hole BBDD-31 returned 7 metres of 7.21 g/t AuEq from 385 metres downhole, including 1 metre at 43.68 g/t AuEq — the highest single-metre grade drilled at BBM and the first systematic confirmation that the deposit's high-grade core continues below the existing 1.71 Moz AuEq inferred resource, pointing to a scalable underground component. Ten more holes from this campaign have assays pending.

headline: SEABRIDGE LOCKS IN US$100M CREDIT LINE FOR KSM 2026 SUMMER PROGRAM — Canada's Largest Undeveloped Au-Cu Deposit Advances Toward Feasibility (TSX: SEA)
snippet: Seabridge Gold (TSX: SEA) arranged a US$100 million unsecured short-term credit facility with an unnamed strategic investor to fund the KSM Project's 2026 summer season in British Columbia — covering road construction and the geotechnical, metallurgical, and environmental data collection required to support feasibility-level design at what remains Canada's largest undeveloped gold-copper deposit. The facility is drawable in minimum US$10 million tranches at 7% interest compounded monthly and matures December 31, 2026, with repayment optionally in shares under specified conditions.

headline: EMINENT GOLD LAUNCHES 10,000m DISCOVERY EXPANSION IN NEVADA — Carlin-Style Oxide System Grows; Phase 2 Attacks Multiple Fault Zones at Hot Springs Range (TSXV: EMNT)
snippet: Eminent Gold Corp. (TSXV: EMNT) mobilized its drill contractor at Hot Springs Range in Humboldt County, Nevada on July 17 and has now commenced a 10,000-metre reverse circulation program targeting expansion of a Carlin-style oxide gold system first confirmed by four diamond core holes — highlighted by 9.2 metres grading 3.2 g/t Au. The program includes 14 RC holes at the Otis target and up to five initial holes at the Eden target, advancing along the Little Humboldt Fault that produced the project's strongest oxide gold interval to date.

headline: GOLD MINERS ENTER NEAR-RECORD Q2 EARNINGS SEASON WHILE TRADING AT DECADE-LOW P/Es — $2,787/oz Implied Q2 Profit vs 20x Multiple; Kinross Reports July 29
snippet: Adam Hamilton's pre-earnings analysis of GDX top-25 gold miners projects implied Q2 2026 profits of approximately $2,787 per ounce — 50% above Q2 2025 and the sector's second-best result ever (after Q1 2026's $3,129) — yet the group trades at just 20.2x trailing P/E, down from 49.6x in late 2023 despite successive record-margin quarters. With Kinross reporting July 29 and most major producers following within two weeks, the pre-earnings case for mean reversion in mining equity multiples is the most specific it has been since the Q1 2026 reporting season.

headline: PHYSICAL GOLD BEATS GDX BY 5 POINTS OVER THREE MONTHS — Motley Fool Asks: Does Miner Leverage Ever Pay Off Against Owning Bullion?
snippet: A Motley Fool analysis published July 18 found that GDX fell 17.4% over the three months ending July 17, 2026 — roughly 5 points worse than GLD's 12.7% decline — illustrating how operational leverage works against mining stocks when gold corrects; over ten years GLD has also outpaced GDX (196.5% vs. 183.2%), and the iShares MSCI Global Gold Miners ETF (RING) has beaten GDX across one-, five-, and ten-year periods. The article does not argue against owning miners, but frames the leverage case more clearly than most retail-focused content: you need to be right about both the gold price AND the timing of the correction.

headline: SHANGHAI SILVER PREMIUM HITS 12% AS CHINA'S PHYSICAL BUYERS DEFY COMEX — Industrial Demand Decouples From Paper Market in Rare Structural Signal
snippet: The Shanghai silver premium over COMEX spot reached 12% during the latest precious metals weekly review, as Chinese industrial buyers — representing roughly 58% of global silver consumption — continued to pay up for physical metal even as Western paper markets reflected Iran-driven oil inflation and rising Fed rate-hike expectations. FindBullionPrices frames the divergence as a binary resolution: either Chinese demand collapses (bearish for silver's structural thesis) or COMEX spot eventually follows Shanghai physical prices higher, consistent with the market's sixth consecutive annual supply deficit.
